summary: Nothing you already have covers every Vaultwise haptic token. expo-haptics 57.0.3 only plays fixed iOS presets: no intensity or sharpness, no continuous or AHAP patterns, no Android Composition, and no GESTURE_THRESHOLD constants. react-native-pulsar 1.7.0 adds iOS Core Haptics patterns and some Android Composition, but it cannot play AHAP files and has no threshold constants. react-native-haptic-feedback 3.0.0 covers threshold constants, intensity and AHAP, but its Android patterns are plain waveforms and SEGMENT_TICK is wired to the wrong API level. Recommendation: keep expo-haptics for system-meaning tokens and build one small custom Expo module (about 450–550 lines, 3–5 engineer-days plus device QA) for the expressive, detent and threshold tokens. Pulsar is fine for prototyping or as a stopgap. On Opal, sources document only a few things: Apple's 2025 Design Award citation praises its haptics when unlocking gems, and its help centre says the haptics are switched off from iOS Settings. App Store reviews add one mention. No founder or designer write-up was found, but social, LinkedIn and press sources were not searched because the shared web-search budget ran out. A phone-on-phone and contact-microphone benchmark protocol is included.

findings.claim: expo-haptics 57.0.3 on iOS exposes only impact styles (light, medium, heavy, soft, rigid), notification types and selection. Every call creates a new generator, calls prepare() and fires immediately. There is no intensity or sharpness argument, no continuous event and no AHAP playback.
findings.evidence: In the package source (ios/HapticsModule.swift in the npm tarball), impactAsync builds UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(style:), then calls prepare() and impactOccurred() back to back. 58.0.5 only migrates to the Expo Modules API 2.0 macros. Apple's prepare() doc says preparing and then firing straight away does not improve latency. impactOccurred(intensity:) has existed since iOS 13 but expo does not expose it.

findings.claim: On Android, expo-haptics impactAsync, notificationAsync and selectionAsync are hand-made Vibrator waveforms (amplitudes 30–70/255, 40–60 ms), not system haptics. performAndroidHapticsAsync wraps View.performHapticFeedback for 19 constants but not GESTURE_THRESHOLD_ACTIVATE or DEACTIVATE. When a constant is missing on an older API level, the promise rejects instead of falling back.
findings.evidence: HapticsImpactType.kt and HapticsNotificationType.kt define the waveforms (for example success is 0,40,100,40 ms). HapticsRecord.kt looks up HapticFeedbackConstants fields by reflection. For anything not in a short always-available list it throws HapticsNotSupportedException. 57.0.2 fixed performAndroidHapticsAsync doing nothing off the main queue.

findings.claim: Exact Android API levels: CONFIRM, REJECT, GESTURE_START and GESTURE_END are API 30. GESTURE_THRESHOLD_ACTIVATE, GESTURE_THRESHOLD_DEACTIVATE, SEGMENT_TICK, SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK, TOGGLE_ON, TOGGLE_OFF, DRAG_START and NO_HAPTICS are API 34. KEYBOARD_PRESS, KEYBOARD_RELEASE, TEXT_HANDLE_MOVE and VIRTUAL_KEY_RELEASE are API 27. CONTEXT_CLICK is 23, CLOCK_TICK 21, KEYBOARD_TAP 8, VIRTUAL_KEY 5, LONG_PRESS 3. FLAG_IGNORE_GLOBAL_SETTING is deprecated in API 33 and only privileged apps can use it.
findings.evidence: Parsed from the 'Added in API level' annotations on the HapticFeedbackConstants reference page. The reference describes GESTURE_THRESHOLD_ACTIVATE and DEACTIVATE as built for pull-to-refresh-style thresholds.

findings.claim: Composition primitives: CLICK, TICK, QUICK_RISE, SLOW_RISE and QUICK_FALL are API 30. THUD, SPIN and LOW_TICK are API 31. addPrimitive(id, scale, delay) is API 30; the delayType overload is API 36. areAllPrimitivesSupported and arePrimitivesSupported are API 30, getPrimitiveDurations 31, hasAmplitudeControl 26. vibrate(effect, VibrationAttributes) and USAGE_MEDIA are API 33; USAGE_TOUCH is API 30. Envelope effects and frequency profiles are API 36.
findings.evidence: Parsed from the VibrationEffect.Composition, Vibrator and VibrationAttributes reference pages. Android's guide says one unsupported primitive makes the whole composition fail silently. It recommends scale steps at a ratio of 1.4 or more, no more than three intensity levels, and gaps of 50 ms or more to be felt. It also says 'Android 16 (26Q4)' adds VibrationEffect.Builder with automatic fallback.

findings.claim: react-native-pulsar 1.7.0 on iOS turns discrete pattern events into Core Haptics transient events with intensity (amplitude) and sharpness (frequency). Continuous envelopes become a continuous event with parameter curves. System presets use UIKit generators that are prepared when the preset is created. There is no AHAP loader in the React Native API, only Pulsar's own JSON pattern format.
findings.evidence: Read in the repo at tag v1.7.0: DiscreteLine.swift, PatternComposer.swift and SystemPresetsImpl.swift. The TurboModule spec has Pulsar_play, PatternComposer_parsePattern/play, RealtimeComposer_set/playDiscrete, preloadPresets, hapticSupport and enableHaptics/enableSound; none of them loads AHAP. The engine wrapper never sets playsHapticsOnly, which Apple says reduces startup latency.

findings.claim: Pulsar on Android only partly supports Composition. Patterns made only of taps compile to VibrationEffect.Composition with scale and delay taken from the pattern, but the primitive is chosen by frequency and can only be CLICK, TICK or LOW_TICK (LOW_TICK only from API 33). Anything with a continuous part becomes an envelope on API 36, an amplitude waveform if the phone has amplitude control, or on/off pulses otherwise. It checks isPrimitiveSupported, but it calls Vibrator.vibrate without VibrationAttributes, so no touch usage is set.
findings.evidence: Read in ImpulseCompositionHapticBuilder.kt (selectPrimitive), VibrationEffectsGenerator.kt and HapticEngineWrapper.kt. The support levels map to: LIMITED (no amplitude control), STANDARD (amplitude control), ADVANCED (API 36 frequency profile).

findings.claim: Pulsar's Android system presets call performHapticFeedback with the right API checks and fall back to a Pulsar pattern. There is no GESTURE_THRESHOLD_ACTIVATE or DEACTIVATE preset, and REJECT is exposed under the name `release`. Its audio simulation is on by default in iOS DEBUG builds and on simulators or emulators, so dev builds can make sound until Settings.enableSound(false) is called.
findings.evidence: SystemViewBasedPresets.kt maps release() to HapticFeedbackConstants.REJECT. The audio default is set by `#if DEBUG _playSound = true` in AudioSimulator.swift; the Android side uses BuildConfig.DEBUG or emulator. The docs require React Native 0.71+ and the New Architecture. The React Native package uses the published core artifacts (iOS pod 1.4.0, Android 1.3.0).

findings.claim: react-native-haptic-feedback 3.0.0 offers impact(type, intensity), triggerPattern with intensity and sharpness, playAHAP(fileName) from the app bundle, and all Android constants including gestureThresholdActivate and Deactivate (API 34, with waveform fallback). Limits: it maps SEGMENT_TICK and SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK under API 30 although they are API 34; Android patterns are waveforms only; it skips haptics when the ringer is silent; on iOS every trigger type is a Core Haptics approximation, not the UIKit system pattern.
findings.evidence: In RNReactNativeHapticFeedbackModuleImpl.java, segmentTick is put in VIEW_HAPTIC_MAP inside `SDK_INT >= R`. VibrateFactory.vibratePattern uses createWaveform with USAGE_TOUCH on API 33+. Its Expo config plugin is a no-op, so .ahap files must be added to the Xcode bundle by hand, which conflicts with Expo's regenerated native folders. Inference: on API 30–33 the decorView path probably does nothing and the waveform fallback is never reached. Needs a device test.

findings.claim: Android battery saver (AOSP main) drops touch, unknown and media vibrations. That covers both performHapticFeedback and ordinary Vibrator calls, so no library can play UI haptics in battery saver.
findings.evidence: In VibrationSettings.java, BATTERY_SAVER_USAGE_ALLOWLIST contains only RINGTONE, ALARM, COMMUNICATION_REQUEST, PHYSICAL_EMULATION and HARDWARE_FEEDBACK. shouldIgnoreVibration returns IGNORED_FOR_POWER for any other usage. HapticFeedbackVibrationProvider gives most constants USAGE_TOUCH, and they go through the same VibratorManagerService pipeline. Phone makers' skins (for example Samsung) may behave differently; this was not verified.

findings.claim: Android touch-feedback settings: performHapticFeedback respects the user's touch feedback setting and needs no VIBRATE permission. A Vibrator effect without attributes is reclassified as USAGE_TOUCH only if it lasts 1000 ms or less and has at most 3 segments. Otherwise it stays USAGE_UNKNOWN and follows the Media vibration setting, so expo's 4–6-segment notification waveforms (and longer Pulsar patterns) are probably not governed by Touch feedback.
findings.evidence: The Android haptic-feedback guide states the first two points. In AOSP, fixupVibrationAttributes calls isHapticFeedbackCandidate (MAX_HAPTIC_FEEDBACK_DURATION = 1000, MAX_HAPTIC_FEEDBACK_COMPOSITION_SIZE = 3). createWaveform makes one StepSegment per timing entry, and USAGE_UNKNOWN uses MEDIA_VIBRATION_INTENSITY. That expo's notification patterns ignore Touch feedback is an inference from that code; verify on devices.

findings.claim: How AOSP renders the key constants: CONFIRM is EFFECT_CLICK, REJECT is EFFECT_DOUBLE_CLICK, GESTURE_THRESHOLD_ACTIVATE and SEGMENT_TICK are EFFECT_TICK, SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK is EFFECT_TEXTURE_TICK, GESTURE_THRESHOLD_DEACTIVATE is PRIMITIVE_TICK at scale 0.4 (or TEXTURE_TICK), TOGGLE_ON is PRIMITIVE_TICK at 0.5 and TOGGLE_OFF is PRIMITIVE_LOW_TICK at 0.2. Phone makers can override these.
findings.evidence: Read in HapticFeedbackVibrationProvider.java, including its getVibration(primitive, scale, fallback) helper and its customization hook.

findings.claim: iOS settings and power: Apple says UIKit and SwiftUI feedback only informs the system, which decides whether to play based on device, app state, remaining battery and other factors. It plays only in the foreground, with the system Haptics setting on, on hardware that supports haptics. Expo's docs say the Taptic Engine does nothing in Low Power Mode, when the user has turned haptics off, while the camera is active, or during dictation. No fetched Apple page says whether Core Haptics follows the System Haptics switch or Low Power Mode.
findings.evidence: Apple's 'Playing haptic feedback in your app' article and the expo-haptics docs (v57). Apple's isLowPowerModeEnabled page does not list haptics among the power-saving measures. iPad does not support haptics per Apple's Core Haptics setup guide, and Vaultwise sets supportsTablet: true.

findings.claim: Core Haptics can play AHAP from a file URL or from Data, play continuous events up to 30 s long, and set sharpness from 0 to 1. Starting the engine before playback avoids a significant delay, and playsHapticsOnly lowers startup latency. With isAutoShutdownEnabled the engine stops after about 2 minutes idle.
findings.evidence: Apple Core Haptics reference pages, read via Apple's JSON documentation endpoints.

findings.claim: Opal fact: Apple's 2025 Design Awards page lists Opal as a Social Impact finalist and specifically praises its haptics when unlocking gems.
findings.evidence: The citation on Apple's 2025 winners and finalists page credits "haptics when unlocking 'gems'" as one of Opal's touches. Opal's own blog (June 6, 2025) confirms the Social Impact finalist status.

findings.claim: Opal fact: Opal's help centre tells users to turn haptics off through iOS Settings, which suggests Opal has no in-app haptics toggle. Its iOS haptics follow the system setting.
findings.evidence: Help article 'How to disable Haptics' links to Apple's 'Turn off vibration on iPhone' guide (Settings > Sounds & Haptics, or Accessibility > Touch > Vibration). Whether Opal uses UIKit generators or Core Haptics is not documented.

findings.claim: Opal fact: of the 2,000 most recent App Store reviews (500 each from US, GB, CA and AU, fetched 2026-10-10), only one explicitly mentions haptics. It is a 4-star US review of version 4.7 (2026-07-27) about feeling haptics when cracking a gem after a focus session. Others praise the 'premium' feel or mention ambient sounds, mini games and sound added in the June 2026 redesign, alongside complaints about lag.
findings.evidence: Apple customer-review RSS feeds. The haptics review is id 14354443371 on US page 7; the 'premium' review is id 14413617805 on US page 5; the sound and mini-game reviews are on AU page 2. The App Store description does not mention haptics. The listing shows an Editors' Choice badge, requires iOS 18.0, and the current version is 4.18.

findings.claim: Opal fact: the founder's naming essay (March 19, 2026) frames the brand around touch, contrasting a phone (glass, aluminium, charged) with a gemstone (cool, rough, organic). It also says he wants Opal to give constant feedback on how users are doing. The Android app declares the 'control vibration' permission, and no Google Play review visible on the listing mentions haptics.
findings.evidence: Opal blog post. The Play Store listing's permission data includes 'control vibration' (android.permission.VIBRATE). This is not proof of a particular haptics design on Android.

findings.claim: Other apps praised for haptics in Apple Design Award citations make defensible benchmark peers: Denim (custom haptics), Vocabulary and PBJ (2025); (Not Boring) Camera (haptic scroll wheels) and PowerWash Simulator (a different haptic per hose nozzle) (2026).
findings.evidence: Found by scanning the 2025 and 2026 ADA winners and finalists pages for 'haptic'. No primary source was found for Robinhood, Duolingo, Revolut or Apple Pay haptics because search was unavailable.

findings.claim: Problems in the existing Vaultwise engine (mobile/src/lib/haptics/engine.ts): multi-step tokens are scheduled with JS setTimeout, so timing can jitter. The Android fallback calls expo impactAsync and notificationAsync, which are Vibrator waveforms. Promise rejections from performAndroidHapticsAsync on older API levels are swallowed, so tokens such as Segment_Tick below API 34 or Confirm/Reject below API 30 silently do nothing.
findings.evidence: Read in the local file mobile/src/lib/haptics/engine.ts, together with the expo-haptics source and the API levels above. Expo SDK 57 sets Android minSdk to 24 (react-native/gradle/libs.versions.toml) and iOS to 16.4 (ExpoModulesCore.podspec).

spec:
# Vaultwise haptics: implementability and the Opal benchmark
Researched 2026-10-10 against Expo SDK 57 (expo-haptics 57.0.3), React Native 0.86.3, react-native-pulsar 1.7.0 and react-native-haptic-feedback 3.0.0.

**How this was researched:** package code comes from the published npm tarballs and the Pulsar repo at tag `v1.7.0`. Android behaviour comes from AOSP `refs/heads/main`; Apple and Android docs were read directly.

**Gap:** the shared web-search budget ran out early, so X/Twitter, LinkedIn, Medium, podcasts, Dribbble/Behance and press were **not searched**. All Opal facts below come from direct fetches of known pages.

---

## Part 1A: Capability × library feasibility

**Libraries compared:**
- **E** = expo-haptics 57.0.3
- **P** = react-native-pulsar 1.7.0
- **R** = react-native-haptic-feedback 3.0.0
- **C** = custom Expo Modules API module

| Capability | E | P | R | C, and what it needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **iOS transient with intensity and sharpness** | **No.** Fixed styles only ([HapticsModule.swift](https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/sdk-57/packages/expo-haptics/ios/HapticsModule.swift)) | **Yes.** `discretePattern {time, amplitude→intensity, frequency→sharpness}` and `RealtimeComposer.playDiscrete` ([DiscreteLine.swift](https://github.com/software-mansion/pulsar/blob/v1.7.0/iOS/Pulsar/Sources/Pulsar/Lines/DiscreteLine.swift)) | **Yes.** `impact(type, intensity)` and `triggerPattern` ([README](https://github.com/mkuczera/react-native-haptic-feedback/tree/v3.0.0)) | **Yes.** `CHHapticEvent(.hapticTransient)` ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corehaptics/chhapticevent/eventtype/haptictransient)) |
| **Generator prepare and latency priming** | **No.** prepare() then fire immediately, which Apple says gives no benefit ([prepare()](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uifeedbackgenerator/prepare())) | **Partial.** System-preset generators are prepared once when created; `Settings.preloadPresets` caches Core Haptics players | **Partial.** Core Haptics engine is started at init; no UIKit priming | **Yes.** Call `prepare()` on press-in or screen mount and re-prepare after each fire; start the engine with `playsHapticsOnly = true` ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corehaptics/chhapticengine/playshapticsonly)) |
| **Continuous events** | **No** | **Yes on iOS** (`continuousPattern` → continuous event with parameter curves). **Android:** envelope on API 36, otherwise amplitude or on/off waveform ([VibrationEffectsGenerator.kt](https://github.com/software-mansion/pulsar/blob/v1.7.0/Android/Pulsar/src/main/java/com/swmansion/pulsar/haptics/VibrationEffectsGenerator.kt)) | **Yes on iOS.** Android: waveform | **Yes.** iOS continuous events up to 30 s ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corehaptics/chhapticevent/eventtype/hapticcontinuous)); Android `SLOW_RISE`, `QUICK_RISE`, or envelopes on API 36 |
| **AHAP playback** | **No** | **No.** Pulsar uses its own JSON pattern format ([NativeRNPulsar.ts](https://github.com/software-mansion/pulsar/blob/v1.7.0/react-native/react-native-pulsar/src/NativeRNPulsar.ts)) | **Yes, as files.** `playAHAP(fileName)` reads from the app bundle; its config plugin is a no-op, so files must be added to Xcode by hand ([app.plugin.js](https://github.com/mkuczera/react-native-haptic-feedback/blob/v3.0.0/app.plugin.js)) | **Yes.** `CHHapticEngine.playPattern(from: Data)` with AHAP JSON sent as a string from JS, so no bundling ([doc](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corehaptics/chhapticengine/playpattern(from:)-7u8se)) |
| **Android Composition: any primitive with per-primitive scale and delay, plus `areAllPrimitivesSupported`** | **No** | **Partial.** Tap-only patterns become a Composition with scale = amplitude and delay = time gap, but only CLICK, TICK or LOW_TICK (LOW_TICK from API 33). Single-primitive presets exist for all 8 primitives, without scale. Support is checked ([ImpulseCompositionHapticBuilder.kt](https://github.com/software-mansion/pulsar/blob/v1.7.0/Android/Pulsar/src/main/java/com/swmansion/pulsar/haptics/ImpulseCompositionHapticBuilder.kt)) | **Partial.** One primitive at a fixed scale for impact types on API 31+; patterns are waveforms only | **Yes.** `startComposition().addPrimitive(id, scale, delay)` (API 30); THUD, SPIN and LOW_TICK are API 31 ([doc](https://developer.android.com/reference/android/os/VibrationEffect.Composition)) |
| **performHapticFeedback constants** | 19 constants. **No GESTURE_THRESHOLD_\***. Missing constants make the promise reject | Most constants, with API checks and pattern fallback. **No GESTURE_THRESHOLD_\***. REJECT is named `release` | **All**, including threshold constants (API 34) with waveform fallback. **Bug:** SEGMENT_TICK and SEGMENT_FREQUENT_TICK are mapped at API 30, but they are API 34 | **Yes.** Full set, with our own fallback table |
| **Amplitude-control detection** | **No** | **Yes.** `Settings.getHapticsSupportLevel()`: LIMITED (no amplitude), STANDARD (amplitude), ADVANCED (API 36 frequency profile) | **No.** `isSupported()` only checks for a vibrator | **Yes.** `hasAmplitudeControl()` (API 26), `arePrimitivesSupported` (API 30), `getPrimitiveDurations` (API 31), `areEnvelopeEffectsSupported` (API 36) |
| **Battery saver and Low Power Mode** | OS-controlled; nothing to detect | Same | Same | Can detect only, via [expo-battery](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/battery/) `isLowPowerModeEnabledAsync()` (already a first-party package; no custom module needed). Do **not** work around it |
| **Respecting system touch-haptics settings** | Android perform constants respect it. Android impact/notification waveforms have no usage set; 4–6-segment ones probably follow **Media** vibration, not Touch | No usage set on the Vibrator path (same caveat). `enableHaptics(false)` gives an in-app off switch | Sets `USAGE_TOUCH` on API 33+. Also silences haptics when the ringer is silent | **Yes.** Set `VibrationAttributes.createForUsage(USAGE_TOUCH)` (API 33) |

### Platform behaviour that limits every library

**Android battery saver (AOSP main)**
- Vibrations are kept only for these usages: RINGTONE, ALARM, COMMUNICATION_REQUEST, PHYSICAL_EMULATION and HARDWARE_FEEDBACK. Everything else gets `IGNORED_FOR_POWER`.
- That includes `USAGE_TOUCH`, which is what most `performHapticFeedback` constants use. So in battery saver **all UI haptics are silent** ([VibrationSettings.java](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/main/services/core/java/com/android/server/vibrator/VibrationSettings.java), [HapticFeedbackVibrationProvider.java](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/main/services/core/java/com/android/server/vibrator/HapticFeedbackVibrationProvider.java)).
- Do not get around this by borrowing ALARM-type usages. Make sure meaning is carried visually.

**Android Touch feedback setting**
- `performHapticFeedback` respects it and needs no VIBRATE permission ([guide](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/haptics/haptic-feedback)).
- A Vibrator effect with no usage set counts as touch only if it is 1000 ms or shorter and has at most 3 segments. Otherwise it follows the Media vibration setting ([VibratorManagerService.java](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/main/services/core/java/com/android/server/vibrator/VibratorManagerService.java), [VibrationEffect.java](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/main/core/java/android/os/VibrationEffect.java)).

**iOS settings, power and context**
- UIKit and SwiftUI feedback plays only in the foreground, only with system Haptics on, and the system also weighs battery level ([Apple](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/applepencil/playing-haptic-feedback-in-your-app)).
- Expo states the Taptic Engine does nothing in Low Power Mode, while the camera is active, or during dictation ([Expo](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/haptics/)).
- **Vaultwise impact:** proof photos and Pay with Vaultwise QR codes both use `expo-camera`. Fire "proof approved" after the camera view closes.
- **Not documented anywhere fetched:** whether Core Haptics obeys the System Haptics switch or Low Power Mode. Test it.

**iPad:** iPad has no haptics ([Apple](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corehaptics/preparing-your-app-to-play-haptics)), and `app.json` has `supportsTablet: true`. Every token needs a visual equivalent.

---

## Part 1B: Token × library matrix and recipes

**How to read this table:**
- **Yes** = done faithfully; **Approx** = possible but degraded; **No** = not possible.
- iOS and Android recipes are **design proposals (inference)**. Their parameter rules follow Android's perceptual guidance: scale steps at a ratio of 1.4 or more, at most 3 intensity levels, gaps of 50 ms or more to be felt ([guide](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/haptics/custom-haptic-effects)).
- Android fallbacks follow AOSP's own mappings (for example CONFIRM = EFFECT_CLICK, REJECT = EFFECT_DOUBLE_CLICK).

| Token | iOS recipe | Android recipe (fallback) | E | P | R | C | Route |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **PIN key tick** | `UIImpactFeedbackGenerator(.light)`, prepared when the keypad appears and re-prepared after each tap | `VIRTUAL_KEY` (API 5) | Approx (no priming on iOS) | Yes | Yes | Yes | E now; C for priming |
| **PIN success** | notification `.success` | `CONFIRM` (API 30); below that, `createPredefined(EFFECT_CLICK)` (API 29) | Yes, with JS fallback | Yes | Yes | Yes | E |
| **PIN failure** | notification `.error` | `REJECT` (API 30); below that, `EFFECT_DOUBLE_CLICK` | Yes, with fallback | Yes (`release`) | Yes | Yes | E |
| **Amount stepper detent** | `UISelectionFeedbackGenerator`, prepared during press-and-hold | `SEGMENT_TICK` (API 34); below that, `CLOCK_TICK` (API 21) | Approx (rejects below 34; JS thread) | Yes (worklet) | Broken on API 30–33 | Yes | C (or P) |
| **Slider threshold** | crossing in: transient intensity 0.7, sharpness 0.8; crossing out: intensity 0.35, sharpness 0.3 | `GESTURE_THRESHOLD_ACTIVATE` / `DEACTIVATE` (API 34); below that, `EFFECT_TICK` / `EFFECT_TEXTURE_TICK` | Approx | Approx | Yes | Yes | C |
| **Pull-to-refresh threshold** | same as slider threshold | same; this constant was designed for pull-to-refresh | Approx | Approx | Yes | Yes | C |
| **Vault contribution "locked"** | 2 transients: 0 ms at intensity 0.3 / sharpness 0.5, then 150 ms at 0.9 / 0.7 (Pulsar's `Lock` preset has the same tap timing, plus a continuous layer) | Composition: TICK 0.5, then CLICK 1.0 after 120 ms (or THUD 1.0 on API 31+); if primitives are unsupported, `EFFECT_HEAVY_CLICK` | Approx (2 impacts via setTimeout; buzzy on Android) | Yes on iOS; Approx on Android | iOS Yes; Android Approx | Yes | C (P `Lock` as interim) |
| **Proof approved** | notification `.success`, fired after the camera closes | `CONFIRM` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | E |
| **Proof routed to human review** | impact `.soft` (neutral, "noted") | `GESTURE_END` (API 30); below that, `CLOCK_TICK` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | E |
| **Declined** | notification `.error` | `REJECT` | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | E |
| **Tier-2 hold start** | continuous intensity 0 → 0.5 over 250 ms, sharpness 0.3, then a transient at 0.6 | `SLOW_RISE` 0.5 then TICK 0.6 after 0 ms; if unsupported, `EFFECT_CLICK` | No | iOS Yes; Android Approx | iOS Yes; Android Approx | Yes | C |
| **Tier-2 countdown end** | transients at 0 ms and 120 ms, intensity 0.8, sharpness 0.6 | CLICK 0.7, then CLICK 1.0 after 100 ms | Approx | Yes | iOS Yes; Android Approx | Yes | C or P |
| **Irreversible-action confirm (firm, distinct)** | while held: continuous ramp intensity 0.2 → 0.8; on commit: transient 1.0 / 1.0, then 0.6 / 0.3 at +60 ms | while held: `QUICK_RISE`; on commit: THUD 1.0 (API 31) or CLICK 1.0; fallback `EFFECT_HEAVY_CLICK` | No | iOS Yes; Android Partial | iOS Yes; Android Approx | Yes | C |
| **Milestone 25%** | 1 transient at intensity 0.5 | CLICK 0.5 | Approx | Yes | iOS Yes; Android Approx | Yes | C or P |
| **Milestone 50%** | 2 transients at 0.5 and 0.7, 90 ms apart | CLICK 0.5, then CLICK 0.7 after 90 ms | Approx | Yes | iOS Yes; Android Approx | Yes | C or P |
| **Milestone 100%** (Full setting only) | 4 transients rising 0.5 → 1.0, 80 ms apart, plus a 300 ms swell | CLICK 0.5 / 0.7 / 1.0 with ≥ 60 ms gaps, plus `QUICK_RISE` (API 30) | Approx | Yes | iOS Yes; Android Approx | Yes | C or P |
| **Streak kept** | 2 transients at intensity 0.4, sharpness 0.6, 80 ms apart | TICK 0.5 twice, 80 ms apart | Approx | Yes | iOS Yes; Android Approx | Yes | C or P |
| **Payment success (neutral)** | single impact `.light`; deliberately not `.success` | `CONFIRM` (= EFFECT_CLICK) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | E |
| **Remaining tokens** (toggle, tab/segment, long-press, limit warning) | selection / impact `.light` / impact `.medium` / notification `.warning` | `TOGGLE_ON` / `TOGGLE_OFF` (API 34, else `CLOCK_TICK`), `LONG_PRESS` (API 3), `REJECT` or `EFFECT_DOUBLE_CLICK` | Yes, with fallbacks | Yes | Yes | Yes | E |

## Recommended architecture

**1. Keep expo-haptics for system-meaning tokens.** That is PIN success/failure, proof approved/review, declined, payment neutral and toggles. Change two things in the existing `engine.ts`:
   - **(a)** On Android, stop falling back to `impactAsync` and `notificationAsync`. Use `performAndroidHapticsAsync` with a JS fallback table keyed on `Platform.Version`: Confirm/Reject/Gesture_* need API 30, Segment_*/Toggle_*/Drag_Start need API 34, otherwise use Clock_Tick, Context_Click or Long_Press.
   - **(b)** Stop silently swallowing rejections; log them in dev builds.

**2. Build a custom Expo module, `modules/vw-haptics`, for the expressive, detent and threshold tokens.** Create it with `npx create-expo-module@latest --local` ([Expo docs](https://docs.expo.dev/modules/get-started/)). Proposed JS API:
   - `capabilities()` returns:
     - **iOS:** `supportsHaptics`
     - **Android:** `{api, hasAmplitudeControl, primitives: Record<Prim, boolean>, primitiveDurations, envelope}`
     - Get Low Power / Power Saver state from expo-battery `isLowPowerModeEnabledAsync()` rather than this module.
   - `prepare(kind)`: iOS only. Keeps impact, selection and notification generators prepared (call on press-in or screen mount).
   - `playTransient(intensity, sharpness)`
     - iOS: Core Haptics.
     - Android: CLICK or TICK, scale from intensity, primitive chosen from sharpness. Fallback `EFFECT_CLICK` / `EFFECT_TICK`.
   - `playPattern(ahapJson)`: iOS `playPattern(from: Data)`, with an engine kept warm (`playsHapticsOnly = true`, restart in `resetHandler` and `stoppedHandler`). Does nothing on Android.
   - `playComposition(steps[{primitive, scale, delayMs}], fallback)`: checks `arePrimitivesSupported` and plays with `USAGE_TOUCH` (API 33+). Later, add `VibrationEffect.Builder` on Android 16 "26Q4", which brings automatic fallback ([guide](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/haptics/custom-haptic-effects)).
   - `perform(constant, fallbackConstant)`: the full constant set, including GESTURE_THRESHOLD_*.

**Effort for the module**

| Piece | Lines | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Swift | ~200–250 | engine lifecycle, generator pool, transient/AHAP/continuous |
| Kotlin | ~180–230 | composition, perform with API checks, capabilities, attributes |
| TypeScript | ~80 | types and token definitions |
| AHAP JSON files | — | one per expressive token |

That is about **3–5 engineer-days**, plus **1–2 days** on a device matrix: iPhone 13–17, Pixel 8–10, a Galaxy S24/S25 and one budget Android without amplitude control. No new permissions: expo-haptics already adds VIBRATE.

**3. Pulsar** is good for prototyping now. Its companion app and 151 presets (Lock, Latch, Clasp, CoinDrop…) help pick feels. It is also a reasonable no-native-code interim for the expressive tokens; it is worklet-compatible, so detents can fire from the UI thread.

It is **not** recommended long-term, for these reasons:
- no AHAP
- Android sequences limited to CLICK, TICK and LOW_TICK
- no threshold constants
- no `USAGE_TOUCH` on the Vibrator path
- debug builds play audio unless `Settings.enableSound(false)` is called
- compatibility with RN 0.86 is unverified (built against 0.81)

**4. Avoid react-native-haptic-feedback 3.0.0** as the main path because of the SEGMENT_TICK mapping bug, ringer-mode gating, iOS approximations of system patterns, and manual AHAP bundling. It is the quickest way to get GESTURE_THRESHOLD_* if the module slips.

**5. Intensity tiers**
- **Subtle:** play only the core tokens, but scale intensity by about 0.7 instead of truncating multi-beat tokens, once the module allows it. Keep scale ratios of 1.4 or more.
- **Full:** everything.
- **Off:** nothing. Apple's HIG asks apps to make haptics optional ([HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/playing-haptics)); Opal has no in-app switch, so this is a differentiator.

**Device tiers (Android)**

| Tier | Condition | Plays |
|---|---|---|
| A | API 31+ and CLICK, TICK, LOW_TICK, THUD, QUICK_RISE and SLOW_RISE all supported | everything |
| B | `hasAmplitudeControl` | perform constants, plus `createPredefined` effects (API 29), plus at most 2-beat waveforms |
| C | no amplitude control | perform constants only; expressive tokens become a single CONFIRM |
| — | API 36 | envelopes allowed for swells |

**iOS:** every iPhone on iOS 16.4+ supports Core Haptics; iPad gets none.

## Part 2: Opal benchmark

### Documented facts (each with its source)

1. **Apple Design Awards 2025, Social Impact finalist.** Apple's citation names its haptics when unlocking gems ([ADA 2025](https://developer.apple.com/design/awards/2025/); [Opal blog, 2025-06-06](https://www.opal.so/blog/apple-design-award-finalist)).
2. **Haptics are switched off only from iOS Settings.** No in-app control is documented ([help article](https://help.opalapp.com/article/how-to-disable-haptics) → [Apple guide](https://support.apple.com/guide/iphone/iphd722c9100/ios)).
3. **App Store reviews.** Of the 2,000 most recent reviews (US, GB, CA, AU), exactly one mentions haptics: gem-cracking after a focus session, v4.7, 2026-07-27 ([RSS US p7](https://itunes.apple.com/us/rss/customerreviews/page=7/id=1497465230/sortby=mostrecent/json)).
   - Others praise the "premium" UI ([US p5](https://itunes.apple.com/us/rss/customerreviews/page=5/id=1497465230/sortby=mostrecent/json)).
   - Others mention sound, ambient sound and mini games after the June 2026 redesign, with lag complaints ([AU p2](https://itunes.apple.com/au/rss/customerreviews/page=2/id=1497465230/sortby=mostrecent/json)).
4. **Founder's essay.** The brand is framed around touch: phone glass and metal versus a cool, rough gemstone, plus a wish to give constant feedback on progress ([blog, 2026-03-19](https://www.opal.so/blog/the-technology-paradox-how-i-named-opal)).
5. **Store listings.**
   - **App Store:** Editors' Choice; requires iOS 18.0; v4.18; the description does not mention haptics ([App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/opal-screen-time-for-focus/id1497465230)).
   - **Android:** declares "control vibration"; no haptic mentions in visible reviews ([Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.withopal.opal)).
6. **Team page.** Lists a Design Engineer, a Creative Director and a Brand Designer; good leads for interviews or posts, not yet searched ([about](https://www.opal.so/about)).

### Not documented
No founder or designer write-up specifically about haptics was found in the pages fetched; social, LinkedIn, podcast, Dribbble/Behance and press sources were not searched. Also unknown: whether Opal uses UIKit generators or Core Haptics, its patterns, its timings, and its Android haptics design.

### Benchmarking protocol (lawful, observational)

**Scope and rules**
- Use your own devices and accounts, and use the apps normally.
- No decompiling, no network interception, no publishing their UI recordings beyond internal analysis.

**Devices**
- One iPhone (15/16/17 class) and one Android flagship (Pixel 9/10, plus a Galaxy S24/S25 if possible).

**Rig 1: phone-on-phone**
- The test phone lies face-up on top of a sensor phone, on foam, held with a rubber band.
- The sensor phone runs [phyphox](https://phyphox.org/) "Acceleration (without g)", controlled from a laptop browser, and exports data.
- Note the sample rate it actually achieved. At about 100 Hz you get timing and envelope only.

**Rig 2: waveform (recommended)**
- A piezo contact microphone taped to the test phone's back, into an audio interface at 48 kHz.
- This captures the actuator waveform and its spectrum (a sharpness proxy).

**Rig 3: latency**
- 240-fps slow-motion video of the screen recorded alongside the piezo audio, to measure the gap between touch and the haptic onset.

**Calibration**
- Build our own reference screen in the dev build that plays known stimuli:
  - iOS: impact light, medium, heavy, soft and rigid; notification success, warning and error; selection; transients at intensity 0.3 / 0.6 / 1.0 × sharpness 0 / 0.5 / 1.0.
  - Android: CLICK, TICK, LOW_TICK and THUD at scale 0.5 / 0.7 / 1.0; CONFIRM, REJECT, SEGMENT_TICK and GESTURE_THRESHOLD_*.
- Record them on the same rig to build a lookup from trace to parameters.

**Interaction scripts (10 repetitions each)**
- **Opal:** start a focus session, choose a duration, end or complete it, crack a gem, hit a block screen, flip toggles, unlock a milestone.
- **Benchmark peers with sourced haptic praise:** (Not Boring) Camera's haptic dials ([ADA 2026](https://developer.apple.com/design/awards/)), Denim ([ADA 2025](https://developer.apple.com/design/awards/2025/)).
- **Payment reference:** Apple Wallet / Apple Pay confirmation.
- **Optional fintech or gamified peers:** Revolut, Duolingo, Robinhood. These are unsourced choices; we found no documentation of their haptics.

**Settings matrix to test**

| Platform | Settings to vary |
|---|---|
| iOS | System Haptics on/off; Accessibility > Touch > Vibration; Low Power Mode on/off; camera active |
| Android | Touch feedback on/off and intensity; Media vibration; battery saver on/off; silent ringer |

**Metrics per event**
- haptic present (yes/no)
- pulse count
- inter-pulse interval (ms)
- total duration
- peak relative to the calibration impacts
- spectral centroid
- latency from touch
- whether it repeats the same way across runs

**Analysis**
- Python with SciPy: envelope threshold detection, onset alignment, a "haptic fingerprint" table per event, then mapping to Vaultwise tokens.

**Perception check**
- 8–12 consenting Gen Z participants, blind A/B: our tokens versus benchmark-inspired variants.
- Rate on 7-point scales: satisfying, premium, annoying, clear meaning.
- Test whether "locked", "approved" and "neutral payment" can be told apart.
